input: Write a letter to my future self for ten years

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A letter can cover anything from career goals to relationships to personal values — knowing which life areas to include shapes the entire structure and length of the letter.

Although addressed to the future self, the letter's intimacy and references change significantly if it is meant to be shared with others (e.g., a partner, family, a time capsule) versus kept completely private.
The user's current life stage — a major transition, a milestone birthday, a new year — sets the emotional backdrop and determines what feels most meaningful to capture right now.
Knowing the desired length (a short paragraph vs. several pages) and any word-count limits prevents over- or under-writing.
Tone — reflective and emotional, motivational and ambitious, humorous and light — fundamentally changes the voice and style of the letter.
Understanding whether the user wants to feel inspired, held accountable, or emotionally moved when they re-read it in ten years defines what 'a great letter' actually means for them.
The intended format (handwritten, digital document, sealed envelope, an online time-capsule service) affects how the letter should be structured and stored.

gold.taskTitle: Write a letter to my future self in ten years
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to compose a personal letter addressed to themselves ten years from now.

questions.title: Which life areas should the letter focus on?
questions.description: Determine whether the letter should cover career, relationships, health, personal growth, finances, or a specific subset of these topics.

questions.title: Is this letter private or meant to be shared?
questions.description: Clarify whether only the user will read it, or if it will be shared with someone else such as a partner, children, or as part of a group time capsule.

questions.title: What is prompting you to write this right now?
questions.description: Understand the current life moment or trigger — a birthday, graduation, new year, major life change — that provides the emotional context for the letter.

questions.title: How long should the finished letter be?
questions.description: Establish a target length, such as a single page, 300–500 words, or a longer multi-page reflection, to guide the level of detail.

questions.title: What tone should the letter carry throughout?
questions.description: Decide whether the letter should feel deeply emotional and reflective, bold and motivational, warm and conversational, or lightly humorous.

questions.title: How do you want to feel re-reading this in ten years?
questions.description: Define the emotional or practical outcome — inspired, nostalgic, held accountable to goals, comforted — so the letter can be written toward that feeling.

questions.title: Where and how will you store or deliver this letter?
questions.description: Determine the intended format — a handwritten sealed envelope, a Word document, an email scheduled for the future, or an online time-capsule service like FutureMe.
